A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ERT research, with matching authors, methods and retained experiments. Text, equations, figures, tables and appendices support comparison despite substantial reorganization.

before.justification: V1 reports original synthetic experiments, classifier comparisons, and conformal-prediction benchmarks for regression and image classification.

after.justification: V2 retains original empirical results and adds classifier-benchmark results, robustness experiments and an isolated investigation of WSC.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 changes aggregation from equally weighted fold estimates to weights proportional to fold size, affecting unequal folds. The classifier-based ERT framework, Table 1 losses and over-/under-coverage decomposition remain.

E1.justification: The classifier study expands from four datasets to eight, adding ailerons, o11, miami2016 and winequality; ailerons and miami already appeared elsewhere in v1. New synthetic scenarios cover smooth and rapidly oscillating heteroscedasticity and varying input dimensions. The existing regression and image-classification benchmark coverage is retained.

E2.justification: V2 adds standardized-residual conformal prediction to the regression comparisons and WSC as a runtime comparator in Table 2. WCovGap disappears from the regression diagnostic comparisons but remains in the synthetic comparison. The seven classifier comparators and the two image-classification strategies are retained.

E3.justification: Regression test allocations increase from approximately 10% to 30%, with v2 specifying a 60/10/30 split; ailerons test samples increase from 1,375 to 4,125. Volume summaries introduce average ranks, and HR's stated internal miscoverage formula loses a factor of two. Added experiments introduce controlled dimension sweeps and evaluation of 90%-coverage oracle sets against an 80% target.

E4.justification: Appendix A adds an isolated WSC sensitivity study across dimensions and sample sizes under perfect conditional coverage. Appendix I adds direct validation of the over-/under-coverage decomposition and smooth versus high-frequency heteroscedasticity stress tests comparing LightGBM with PartitionWise. These address diagnostic behavior beyond v1's existing comparisons.

E5.justification: V2 adds error bars to aggregate regression plots in Figures J.1, J.2, J.4 and J.5, whose v1 counterparts used plain bars, although their statistical meaning is not clearly specified. Both versions already report ten runs and standard deviations in Table 2; an increase in replication is not established.

E6.justification: Table 2 aggregates and regression results are extensively revised, with new standardized-residual results and runtime entries and removal of regression WCovGap results. For example, CASP C-PCP L1-ERT changes from 0.0028 to 0.1154 under revised evaluation settings, not a matched performance comparison. New stress-test findings are added, while synthetic Table 3 values and image-classification results remain unchanged.

T1.justification: V1 Appendix B becomes Appendix C and corrects the convex generator to negative Bayes risk, repairing signs and inequalities in the proper-score construction and Bregman-divergence proof. Appendix A adds an expectation/infimum argument for WSC bias and a cited dimension-dependent bound. Proposition 3.1 and its proof are retained, with the proof relocated.

C1.justification: The abstract corrects the detection condition from 'any classifier' to 'some classifier,' changing its logical quantifier. The introduction explicitly emphasizes the previously established lower-bound property. The main ERT, decomposition, benchmarking and software contributions retain their scope.

C2.justification: V2 explains WSC's downward bias and the L1/L2 scale difference, and adds guidance for other modalities and a caveat about undertraining with larger test allocations. The coverage-size tradeoff remains. C-PCP changes from 'best' to 'one of the best,' but that interpretation still conflicts with its revised aggregate ERT ranking.

D1.justification: V2 newly identifies TabICLv2 as the regression ERT evaluator, states WSC's delta=0.1, explains benchmark normalization, and reports conformal-method runtimes. Hardware reporting narrows from several CPU/GPU types to V100 and eight-core Xeon. Code-access links and most classifier implementation details are retained; newly identifying the regression evaluator does not establish what v1 used.

R1.justification: V2 adds references to TabICLv2 and vision, graph and language benchmarks to support classifier-selection guidance. The positioning against partition-based diagnostics and the connection to Gibbs et al. remain. Numerous other title, year and venue updates concern already cited works.

P1.justification: The narrative is substantially reorganized: conformal background, the Proposition 3.1 proof, classifier curves and detailed regression/classification benchmarking move into reorganized appendices. V2 adds an appendix contents list, condenses the main benchmark discussion and expands explanations of diagnostic interpretation and experimental aggregation.

P2.justification: V2 adopts a two-column main text, redraws and relocates existing figures, and groups Table 3 by diagnostic failure type. It adds robustness plots and coverage-versus-volume scatterplots, reorganizes regression charts, adds error bars, and replaces WCovGap columns with runtime columns in detailed regression tables.

improvement.justification: V2 corrects v1's Bregman-proof sign errors, adds targeted robustness evidence and documents evaluation settings more clearly. These gains are tempered by inconsistent revised regression reporting: the favorable C-PCP discussion conflicts with its aggregate ERT ranking, and Figures J.2/J.5 describe normalized volumes while plotting ranks. The net improvement is useful but qualified.
